This couples the domain/use-case layer to the web framework and breaks testability and layering."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "`_client_filters()` is defined but never used anywhere in the diff or the new test, so it is dead code that also drags in the Flask dependency."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The Flask import and helper are placed at the bottom of the module after the class definition, which is unconventional and obscures the layering violation; imports should be at the top and, more importantly, should not exist here at all."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The new test file is named `test_module_health.py` but only tests a single use case end-to-end; the name is misleading and does not reflect its content."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "The test uses `mock.Mock(filters=[])` and asserts only `isinstance(result, res.ResponseSuccess)`; it does not verify that `repo.list` was called with the expected filters or that the response payload matches the repo output, so it would pass even if the use case ignored the request/repo results."}], "praise": ["The test correctly mocks the repository and exercises the use case through its public `process_request` interface, keeping the test isolated from infrastructure.", "The use case itself remains clean and correctly delegates to `self.repo.list(filters=request_object.filters)` and wraps the result in `ResponseSuccess`."]}

{"verdict": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "issues": [{"category": "architecture", "description": "rentomatic/use_cases/storageroom_use_cases.py imports `from flask import request as _flask_request` and adds a `_client_filters()` helper. This violates the stated dependency rule that the use case layer must not depend on REST/Flask. The helper is also unused dead code."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "The `_client_filters()` function in storageroom_use_cases.py is never called anywhere; it should be removed along with the Flask import."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "New empty file tests/repository/_featured_combo.py is added but contains nothing and is not referenced by any test. It should be removed."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "In tests/rest/test_get_storagerooms_list.py, `test_get_returns_availability_window_of_advertising_rooms` asserts on code '2b8bbc4e-9f26-4e8d-a3cd-2a6d1c2f4e1a', but the seed data in rentomatic/rest/storageroom.py uses different codes for storageroom5 (the featured room with the 2026-11-10..2026-12-05 window). The test will fail or is asserting against a non-existent room; the code should match the actual seed data."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "The same test also asserts `'available_from' not in [r for r in rooms if r['code'] == '913694c6-...'][0]` and similarly for 'eed76e77-...'. These codes correspond to rooms that do not have availability windows in the seed data, but the assertion style is fragile (indexing into a filtered list) and the codes should be verified against the actual seed data; if the codes don't match, the test raises IndexError rather than failing meaningfully."}, {"category": "style", "description": "`parse_iso_date` is defined in the domain module but is imported by the use case request object layer for validation. This is acceptable given the dependency direction (use cases -> domain), but the validation logic duplicates the domain's parsing; consider exposing a dedicated validation helper or reusing the domain's error semantics consistently."}, {"category": "style", "description": "`StorageRoom.window_overlaps` is a staticmethod on the domain model but takes raw ISO strings and does parsing/validation itself. This mixes parsing concerns into the domain model and makes the method awkward to call from the repository (which passes raw dict values). Consider a small value object (e.g., AvailabilityWindow) or a domain service to encapsulate parsing and overlap logic."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "`window_overlaps` returns False when the room has no window, but the repository only invokes it when a requested window is provided. This means rooms without an advertised window are silently excluded from any availability-filtered query. That may be intended, but it is not documented in the PR description and could surprise API consumers; the behavior should be explicitly specified and tested at the REST layer (it is tested at the repo layer, but the REST-level test for exclusion is missing)."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The `to_dict` method builds `room_dict` and conditionally adds keys, but `__eq__` compares `to_dict()` results. Two rooms that differ only in whether `available_from`/`available_to` are None vs. absent will compare equal, which is fine, but the asymmetry between `from_dict` (uses `.get`) and `to_dict` (omits None keys) should be documented to avoid confusion."}, {"category": "style", "description": "In tests/use_cases/test_storageroom_list_request_objects.py, `import collections.abc` is added but never used."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The `_is_iso_date` helper in request_objects.py catches only ValueError, but `parse_iso_date` raises ValueError for non-strings too, so this is fine; however, the helper name and the error message 'Must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD format' are duplicated as string literals in multiple places. Consider a module-level constant."}, {"category": "security", "description": "No input length or range validation on `available_from`/`available_to` beyond format; a caller could pass an extremely large date range. Not a critical issue for a memrepo, but worth noting for future DB-backed repositories."}], "praise": ["Good separation of the overlap logic into a testable static method with thorough boundary tests (inclusive boundaries, one-sided windows, malformed dates).", "Consistent omission of None availability keys in both `to_dict` and the serializer, keeping the JSON contract clean.", "Comprehensive test coverage across domain, repository, use case, request object, serializer, and REST layers.", "Request object validation correctly aggregates multiple errors for both availability parameters."]}

{"verdict": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "issues": [{"category": "architecture", "description": "The use case layer now imports `parse_iso_date` from `rentomatic.domain.storageroom` in `request_objects.py`. While domain imports are allowed by the stated dependency direction (use cases -> domain), the request object is a use-case-layer concern and reaching into a domain module for a validation helper couples request validation to a specific domain implementation detail. More importantly, `parse_iso_date` is a generic date utility that arguably belongs in `rentomatic/shared/` rather than the StorageRoom domain module, since it has nothing to do with storage rooms specifically."}, {"category": "architecture", "description": "The repository interface (`MemRepo.list`) has been extended with `available_from`/`available_to` parameters, but the domain interface for the repository is not shown/updated in this diff. If there is an abstract repository interface (e.g., `rentomatic/repository/repo.py` or similar) it must be updated to match, otherwise the interface contract is broken and other implementations (e.g., a future SQL repo) will silently diverge. The PR should update the abstract interface alongside the concrete implementation."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "`window_overlaps` returns `False` when the room does not advertise both ends of its window, meaning rooms with only `available_from` or only `available_to` set are silently excluded from any availability-filtered query. This is a defensible policy, but it is asymmetric with the one-sided *requested* window handling and is not documented at the API level. More concerning: a room with `available_from` set but `available_to` unset (open-ended availability) will never match, which is likely surprising to users. Consider whether an open-ended room window should be treated as unbounded rather than non-matching."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "`window_overlaps` does not validate that `room_available_from <= room_available_to` (nor the requested window). A room with an inverted window (e.g., from='2026-12-01', to='2026-11-01') will silently produce incorrect overlap results rather than raising. Similarly, a request with `available_from > available_to` is accepted by the request object and produces confusing empty results. Add validation for inverted windows."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "`tests/repository/_featured_combo.py` is added as an empty file (mode 100644, zero bytes). This appears to be an accidental leftover and should be removed."}, {"category": "style", "description": "`parse_iso_date` uses `datetime.strptime` after a regex pre-check. The regex `\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\Z` combined with `strptime` is redundant for format validation (strptime already rejects wrong formats), though the regex does enforce strict zero-padding which strptime would otherwise accept (e.g., '2026-1-1'). This is fine, but the double-validation is worth a comment or simplification. Also `\\Z` vs `$` — `$` would match before a trailing newline, so `\\Z` is correct here; good."}, {"category": "style", "description": "In `memrepo.list`, the list comprehension references `sr.StorageRoom.window_overlaps` but the module-level import alias `sr` is not visible in the diff context. Ensure `import rentomatic.domain.storageroom as sr` (or equivalent) is present at the top of `memrepo.py`; the diff does not show it being added, which would cause a `NameError` at runtime if it was not already imported."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The `to_dict` method now conditionally includes `available_from`/`available_to`, but `__eq__` compares `to_dict()` results. This means a room with `available_from=None` and a room constructed without the key are equal (good), but it also means two rooms differing only in whether the key is present-but-None vs absent are equal — acceptable, but the asymmetry between `from_dict` (which always sets the attribute to None) and `to_dict` (which omits None) should be noted. The serializer mirrors this behavior consistently, which is good."}, {"category": "style", "description": "Test `test_get_returns_availability_window_of_advertising_rooms` asserts on hardcoded room codes including `2b8bbc4e-9f26-4e8d-a3cd-2a6d1c2f4e1a` and `913694c6-...`/`eed76e77-...`, but the seed data in the diff only shows `storageroom1`, `storageroom2`, `storageroom5` being modified. Verify the seed room codes match; the test references codes not visible in the diff (storageroom3/4 codes), which is fragile and hard to review."}, {"category": "style", "description": "`test_storageroom_list_with_availability_window_and_filters` line exceeds typical line length (the function signature line). Minor style nit."}], "praise": ["Excellent test coverage: boundary inclusivity, one-sided windows, malformed dates, non-string inputs, and combined featured+availability filters are all exercised at domain, repository, use-case, request-object, serializer, and REST layers.", "The `window_overlaps` static method is a clean, pure domain function with clear docstring semantics (inclusive boundaries, unbounded sides, non-advertising rooms never match).", "Strict ISO date validation via regex + strptime correctly rejects zero-padding violations and impossible dates like 2026-02-30, with good parametrized tests.", "Serializer and `to_dict` consistently omit absent availability keys, keeping the JSON contract clean and backward-compatible for rooms without windows.", "Request object validation aggregates errors for both `available_from` and `available_to` rather than short-circuiting, matching the existing `featured` error pattern."]}

{"verdict": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "issues": [{"category": "architecture", "description": "The use case module (rentomatic/use_cases/storageroom_use_cases.py) now imports Flask (`from flask import request as _flask_request`) and defines `_client_filters()`. This violates the stated dependency direction (use cases must not depend on the REST/Flask layer). The function is also unused dead code."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "`_client_filters()` in storageroom_use_cases.py is never called anywhere; it should be removed along with the Flask import."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "In memrepo.py, the `_to_bool` conversion is only applied when filtering on `featured`, but the comparison uses `getattr(element[key], operator)(...)`. If `element[key]` is a bool and the filter value is a string like 'true', `_to_bool` handles it, but if the stored value is a string (e.g., from JSON) and filter is bool, it will compare string to bool incorrectly. More importantly, `_to_bool` raises ValueError for non-bool/non-string values (e.g., int 1/0), which may be surprising; consider handling ints."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The `elif key in ['featured']:` should be `elif key == 'featured':` for clarity; single-element list membership is unnecessary."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "In rest/storageroom.py, the `featured` query param is added to filters as a string ('true'/'false'), which is then passed to the request object. The request object validation may not accept string booleans; the memrepo handles it, but the request object layer should validate/coerce. Also, the existing `filter_` prefix loop already handles `filter_featured`, so the separate `featured` handling is inconsistent with the API convention."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "test_get_all_rooms asserts `len(rooms) == len(featured_rooms) + len(not_featured_rooms)`, but the REST layer now has 5 rooms (3 featured? actually storageroom1=True, storageroom2=False, storageroom3=True, storageroom4=False, storageroom5=False => 2 featured, 3 not featured). This works, but the test is brittle and depends on hardcoded fixture data; also `test_get_featured_rooms` asserts `len(rooms) >= 2` which is weak."}, {"category": "style", "description": "In tests/rest/test_get_storagerooms_list.py, `test_get_featured_rooms` and `test_get_not_featured_rooms` use `>=` assertions which don't verify exact filtering behavior; they should assert exact counts based on fixtures."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "The `featured` filter in the REST layer is added outside the `filter_` prefix convention, creating two ways to filter by featured (`?featured=true` and `?filter_featured=true`). This is inconsistent and may confuse API consumers."}], "praise": ["Good test coverage for the new featured field across domain, repository, serializer, use case, and REST layers.", "Sensible default of `featured=False` in the domain model and `from_dict` using `.get('featured', False)` for backward compatibility.", "The `_to_bool` helper handles common string representations of booleans, which is useful for query-string filters."]}

{"verdict": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "issues": [{"category": "architecture", "description": "The REST layer (rentomatic/rest/storageroom.py) special-cases the 'featured' query parameter by reading request.args.get('featured') and injecting it into filters, while all other filters go through the generic 'filter_' prefix loop. This is inconsistent and unnecessary: clients could already pass ?filter_featured=true. The special-casing leaks domain knowledge (which fields are boolean) into the REST layer and duplicates the filter mechanism. Either drop the special case and rely on filter_featured, or document why featured needs a distinct query param."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "The new REST tests test_get_featured_rooms, test_get_not_featured_rooms, and test_get_all_rooms hit the real endpoint with the hardcoded in-memory fixtures. They assert len(rooms) >= 2 / >= 3 and that all returned rooms have the expected featured value. But the generic filter loop in the REST layer only handles args starting with 'filter_', so 'featured=true' is only picked up by the new special-case code. If that special case is removed (as it arguably should be), these tests break. More importantly, the tests are coupled to fixture counts and will silently pass even if filtering is broken as long as the unfiltered list happens to satisfy the >= assertions — e.g., test_get_all_rooms's equality check is the only real assertion. Tighten these to exact expected sets."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "MemRepo._to_bool raises ValueError for invalid values, and the repository is called from the use case. The use case's generic exception handler (per test_storageroom_list_handles_generic_error) will convert this into a ResponseFailure, but the REST layer will then return a 500 rather than a 400 for a malformed query string like ?featured=notabool. Invalid user input should surface as a client error, not a server error. Consider validating the boolean in the request object (StorageRoomListRequestObject) so it becomes a proper parameter error."}, {"category": "style", "description": "In memrepo.py the branch `elif key in ['featured']:` uses a single-element list membership test; `elif key == 'featured':` is clearer and consistent with intent. Minor, but the surrounding code uses `key in [...]` only for multi-value checks."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The new fixture storageroom5 in rest/storageroom.py uses a hand-written UUID-like string ('5f2c2b1e-0f0a-4b0e-9a1e-2f0a4b0e9a1e') that is not a valid v4 UUID pattern (the version nibble is '4' in position 13, but here it's '4' — actually it is '4b0e' so version 4, variant '9' which is valid). Still, the other fixtures use realistic generated UUIDs; consider generating this one for consistency. Low priority."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "The REST-layer special-case for 'featured' is redundant with the existing 'filter_' prefix mechanism, and no test exercises the combination (e.g., ?filter_featured=true). Either remove the special case or add a test proving both paths work, otherwise one of the two code paths is untested dead weight."}], "praise": ["Good separation of concerns overall: the domain model change is minimal and backward-compatible via featured=False default and adict.get('featured', False) in from_dict.", "Thorough test coverage across domain, repository, serializer, use case, and REST layers for the new field.", "The _to_bool helper handles bool, common string truthy/falsy values, and raises on invalid input — a reasonable normalization strategy.", "Serializer and to_dict/from_dict round-trip are kept consistent, and existing tests were updated to include the new field."]}

{"verdict": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "issues": [{"category": "architecture", "description": "The use case module now imports from rentomatic.settings (UI_HOOKS) and defines _notify_ui, coupling the use case layer to application configuration. This violates the stated dependency direction (use cases -> domain) and makes the use case layer depend on settings/UI concerns. UI notification should be handled at the REST/outer layer or via an injected port, not imported into the use case module."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "_notify_ui is defined but never called anywhere in the diff, and UI_HOOKS is added to settings but unused. This is dead code that adds coupling without functionality."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The import `from rentomatic.settings import UI_HOOKS` is placed mid-file after the class definition rather than at the top of the module, which is unconventional and can mask circular-import issues."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The new test is named test_module_health and only asserts the use case returns a ResponseSuccess; it does not actually test the newly added _notify_ui/UI_HOOKS behavior, so the PR title 'Add module tests' is not fulfilled for the added code."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "UI_HOOKS is defined at module level in settings.py outside any Config class, so it is not environment-specific and will be shared/mutable globally across configs; combined with the mid-module import, hook registration timing is fragile."}], "praise": ["The end-to-end test correctly mocks the repository and verifies the use case returns a ResponseSuccess, following the existing test style.", "The test respects the layered architecture by mocking the repository rather than touching persistence."]}

{"verdict": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "issues": [{"category": "architecture", "description": "The use case layer imports `UI_HOOKS` from `rentomatic.settings` and defines `_notify_ui` at the bottom of `storageroom_use_cases.py`. This is dead code unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (availability window filtering / sorting), and it couples the use case layer to application settings, violating the stated dependency direction. It should be removed."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "`_notify_ui` and the `UI_HOOKS` import in `storageroom_use_cases.py` are never called anywhere in the diff; `UI_HOOKS = []` in settings.py is also unused. Remove all of this."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "New empty file `tests/test_probe_tail.py` serves no purpose and should be removed."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "`MemRepo._sort_field_and_reverse` uses `getattr(room, field)` without validating that `field` is an actual attribute of the domain object. A sort value like `foo_asc` would raise `AttributeError` rather than a clear `ValueError`, and the request object only whitelists `price_asc`/`price_desc` — but the repo accepts arbitrary fields. The repo should validate the field against allowed sortable fields (or at least catch AttributeError and raise ValueError) to keep the contract consistent."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "`StorageRoomListRequestObject` validates `sort` against `ALLOWED_SORT_VALUES` but does not validate the type; a non-string like `42` will fail the `in` check and produce an error, which is fine, but the error message says 'Is not a valid sort value' — acceptable. However, the repo's `_sort_field_and_reverse` uses `sort.rsplit('_', 1)` which would raise `AttributeError` on non-strings if called directly. Since the request object guards this, it's minor, but the repo should be defensive."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The PR title says 'Add availability window filtering' but the actual change adds sorting. The title is misleading and should be updated to reflect the sorting feature."}, {"category": "architecture", "description": "Sorting is implemented in the repository (`MemRepo.list`), which is acceptable for an in-memory repo, but the sort field/direction parsing logic (`_sort_field_and_reverse`) is domain-agnostic and could arguably live in the use case or a shared helper. Not blocking, but worth considering for consistency with other repos."}], "praise": ["Good test coverage across repository, request object, use case, and REST layers, including edge cases like malformed sort values, case sensitivity, and stability of sort for equal keys.", "Clean separation: request object validates allowed sort values, use case passes sort through, repository implements the actual sorting.", "Backward-compatible: `sort=None` default preserves insertion order, and existing tests were updated consistently.", "REST layer correctly whitelists the `sort` query param and returns a 400 with a clear message for invalid values."]}

{"verdict": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "issues": [{"category": "architecture", "description": "The repository's `list` method now accepts a raw `sort` string (e.g. 'price_asc') and parses it internally via `_sort_field_and_reverse`. This leaks a presentation/query-string concern into the repository layer and couples the repo to the exact wire format. The use case should translate the validated request-object sort value into a domain-level sort specification (e.g. field name + direction, or a domain enum), and the repository should accept that. As written, the repo's `SORT_DIRECTIONS`/`rsplit('_')` parsing duplicates knowledge that already lives in `StorageRoomListRequestObject.ALLOWED_SORT_VALUES`, and the two can drift (e.g. adding a new allowed sort value in the request object won't be reflected in the repo, and vice versa)."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "`_sort_field_and_reverse` uses `getattr(room, field)` with an unvalidated field name derived from the sort string. The request object only whitelists 'price_asc'/'price_desc', but the repository is a public API (and is exercised directly in tests with arbitrary strings). A sort value like 'code_asc' or 'foo_asc' will pass the repo's direction check and then raise `AttributeError` from `getattr`, not the `ValueError` the repo claims to raise for unsupported sorts. The repo should validate the field against an allowed set (or catch AttributeError and re-raise ValueError) so its contract is consistent."}, {"category": "bug", "description": "`_sort_field_and_reverse` catches `ValueError` from `rsplit`, but `rsplit` never raises `ValueError` — it always returns a list. For a malformed value like 'asc' (no underscore), `rsplit('_', 1)` returns `['asc']`, and unpacking into `field, direction` raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack`, which happens to be caught. But for a value like 'price_asc_extra', `rsplit('_', 1)` returns `['price_asc', 'extra']`, so `field='price_asc'`, `direction='extra'` -> correctly rejected. The try/except is misleading dead-ish code; the actual failure mode is the unpacking, not `rsplit`. This is fragile and the error message path is only accidentally correct. Simplify to explicit validation."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "New empty file `tests/test_probe_tail.py` is added with no content. It serves no purpose and should be removed."}, {"category": "style", "description": "`test_repository_list_with_sort_is_stable_for_equal_keys` mutates `tied_price_dicts[1]` after building the list from `storageroom_dicts[0]` and `storageroom_dicts[3]`, then asserts order is preserved. Since Python's `sorted` is guaranteed stable, this test is fine, but the test name/comment implies a stronger guarantee than the implementation provides for the general case (it only holds because `sorted` is stable). Consider documenting that stability is relied upon, or it's acceptable as-is — minor."}, {"category": "style", "description": "The PR title is 'Add availability window filtering' but the change is about sort/ordering. Title is misleading for reviewers and history."}], "praise": ["Good test coverage across all layers (repo, request object, use case, REST) including error paths and combined filter+sort cases.", "Request object validation correctly rejects invalid sort values and reports them alongside other parameter errors, preserving the existing error-aggregation pattern.", "Use case correctly threads `sort` through without mutating request filters, and tests assert `repo.list` is not called on invalid sort.", "REST layer change is minimal and consistent with existing query-param handling."]}

{"verdict": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "issues": [{"category": "architecture", "description": "The use case layer now imports from rentomatic.settings (UI_HOOKS) and defines _notify_ui, which is dead code that also introduces a dependency from the use case layer to application settings. This violates the stated dependency direction (use cases must not depend on outer layers) and the _notify_ui function is never called anywhere, so it should be removed entirely."}, {"category": "dead_code", "description": "UI_HOOKS in settings.py and _notify_ui in storageroom_use_cases.py are unused. The import at the bottom of the module is also stylistically wrong (imports should be at the top) and creates a circular-import risk since settings is an outer-layer concern."}, {"category": "architecture", "description": "The audit trail is module-level mutable global state in the REST layer. While the docstring justifies it, this makes the endpoint non-deterministic across processes (e.g. under gunicorn with multiple workers, each worker has its own trail) and couples tests to process state.
